m25_fixture.retention_note: Retained text and layout buffer capacities, not process memory. Layout includes rendered text, row offsets, and faces. Text excludes card and thought backing stores. Both exclude block objects, carry strings, indexes, frame buffers, allocator overhead, and temporary allocations. after_browse follows a draw at the first row, which lays out every block; after_follow returns to the live end and draws again.

note: Frames render into a buffer and diff against the last one, the work the live interface does before the terminal write; the size query, the escape encoding, and the write stay outside. frame is one redraw with no new content, the floor of a frame; frame-selected is the same redraw with a drag selection that spans every transcript row; ingest pushes the stream with no frames; stream pushes it with a frame every 64 deltas and is frame-bound, so its throughput is frames per second. Legacy names retain their original fixtures. The -m25 benches use a separate mixed fixture with code, cards, and thinking. frame-m25 draws its mixed tail; stream-m25 appends code-heavy markdown. reflow-m25 alternates widths 120 and 80, including buffer resize and one draw. editor-edit-m25 replaces the empty editor with eight lines and draws once. frame-filled-editor-m25 redraws that filled editor with cached layout. The near browse case keeps 400 capped cards and starts 400 collapsed rows above the end; the cap case keeps 2,000 cards and starts at the first row. Separate browse-expand and browse-collapse distributions change all cards and draw once. Each expansion starts with fresh collapsed layouts. Each collapse starts after an untimed expansion/draw at the same anchor. Fixture creation, anchor setup, opposite-state preparation, and drop stay outside timing; the timed draw includes layouts changed by the operation. frame-browse measures the cached, collapsed state.
